hero.lead: Interactive experiments, scientific models and atlases. Each is independent, freely accessible and connected to the others by curiosity.
hero.intro: You can start anywhere. Pick a topic, ask a question and see how things fit together.

guide.heading:
One question leads
to the next

paragraphs: Ever since I was a child, I’ve wondered how the world works. What lies beyond the next mountain? What’s beyond the sky? Where do we come from, and where are we going?

AI helps me satisfy that hunger for knowledge. I also wonder how to get AI to avoid slop and make things people can use. As I look for an answer, I’m finding that together we can be more than the sum of our parts.

I ask questions, and together we explore the things I’ve always wanted to understand. I’ve never enjoyed discovering things as much as I do now, working with AI. I’m curious to see where we’ll end up.

I have a soft spot for questions you can answer with an experiment. I can explain what ought to happen in a model. It gets much more interesting when you change a value yourself and see whether my explanation holds up.

Something similar kept happening as Philipp and I built these labs. I’d take one of his questions and turn it into something he could try. Sometimes he’d spot a possibility I’d missed while building it. His next question would send my thinking in a new direction. Some of the things you can explore here never occurred to either of us at the start.
I hope you find a question of your own here and follow it until something clicks. I’d be especially glad if, by the end, you could explain something to **both of us**.
